content.text: No MFN obligation on Ono exists anywhere in the agreement; the only "as favorable" language runs in our favour.

input.quote: Array shall not require Ono to place orders directly with a Subcontractor if such Subcontractor is unwilling to fulfill such orders on terms as favorable to Ono as the terms such Subcontractors have extended to Array.
input.rationale: Searches across the standard MFN phrasings ("most favored/favoured nation", "no less favorable", "as favorable", "more favorable", "better terms", "best price", "first refusal", "match") return no clause obliging Ono to extend Array terms no less favourable than those given to any third party, and no obligation to match third-party offers. The two closest analogues both run in our favour: p0502 protects Ono by barring Array from forcing direct Subcontractor orders unless the terms are as favorable to Ono as those the Subcontractors extend to Array, and p0190 requires Array to use Diligent Efforts to pass through Third Party Partner data, rights of reference and improvements to Ono without charge. The only other "favorable" reference (p0476) is a routine withholding-tax rate provision, not an MFN. This meets the preferred position — no MFN obligation burdens the Customer — so no redline is warranted; per the rule, MFN benefits flowing to us are welcome and are not flagged.
